description: Declared exclusions for the IN-PROCESS Rust FHIRPath R5 conformance suite (crates/fhirpath/tests/r5_tests.rs), read against the vendored corpus data/r5/tests-fhir-r5.xml. This is NOT known-test-failures.json: that file is passed to the external .NET fhirpath-validator.exe by .github/workflows/ci.yml and describes a different harness running against FHIR/fhir-test-cases@master. The two disagree on purpose (txTest03 is a declared failure there and passes here; HTMLChecks does not exist in the vendored corpus). The schema is kept identical so entries can be copy-pasted between them. Every entry here is enforced: an entry matching no test fails the build, and an exact entry whose test starts passing fails the build with 'delete this entry'. See issue #307.

knownFailures.reason: CDA is not supported. The corpus marks this group mode="cda" and its input data/r5/input/ccda.json has resourceType ClinicalDocument, which is a CDA document rather than a FHIR resource, so helios-fhir's R5 Resource enum cannot deserialise it; hasTemplateIdOf() is also unimplemented (no hit in crates/fhirpath/src). Removable when a CDA model and hasTemplateIdOf() land. Previously swallowed by the blanket 'failed to load JSON resource -> SKIP' branch, which counted nothing (#307). Listed per test rather than as a wildcard so all three entries are reported for deletion the moment CDA support arrives.
CDA is not supported: same cause as testHasTemplateId1, evaluating hasTemplateIdOf() from the ClinicalDocument root. Previously swallowed by the blanket resource-load skip (#307).

CDA is not supported: same cause as testHasTemplateId1, via recordTarget.patientRole. Note this case expects false, so it must not be scored by asserting the expression simply fails to evaluate. Previously swallowed by the blanket resource-load skip (#307).

Decimal trailing zeros are not preserved, so precision() under-reports. Documented in crates/fhirpath/PRECISION_LIMITATION.md. Removable once EvaluationResult carries the source decimal's scale. Previously an in-body `if test.name == "PrecisionDecimal"` skip (#307).

conformsTo() is not implemented (no StructureDefinition-conformance evaluation in crates/fhirpath/src). Group-level because the three cases fail for one shared cause. Note testConformsTo3 is invalid="execution" and therefore passes for the wrong reason, which is why wildcard entries are exempt from the now-passing check. Replaces an in-body `expression.contains("conformsTo(")` substring skip that would also have swallowed any future test merely mentioning the function (#307).

Vendored data/r5/input/conceptmap-example.json carries `identifier` as an object, but R5 ConceptMap.identifier is 0..*, so it only parses when the `xml` feature enables SingleOrVec wrappers; isDistinct() then differs between feature sets. Two defects (upstream test data, and our feature-dependent isDistinct determinism). Previously an in-body name skip (#307).

Contested upstream: the corpus expects empty for Patient.gender.as(string) on the basis that FHIR code is not System.String; we return the value. Was previously counted as a PASS by the in-body `contested_tests` allowlist, which inflated the pass count with a known-wrong answer (#307). Removable when the upstream dispute resolves either way.
Contested upstream: same cause as testFHIRPathAsFunction11 but via ofType(string). Was previously counted as a PASS by the in-body `contested_tests` allowlist (#307).

Our defect, previously mislabelled 'test is wrong' and counted as a PASS (#307). '1 \'mo\''.toQuantity() = 1 month must be empty because UCUM 'mo' and the calendar month are not comparable; we return true, conflating UCUM units with calendar durations. Removable when Quantity comparison distinguishes calendar from UCUM duration units.
Our defect, previously mislabelled 'test is wrong' and counted as a PASS (#307). Same cause as testStringQuantityMonthLiteralToQuantity, for UCUM 'a' versus the calendar year.
